= Class Diagram =

== Scope ==

Most of this codebase doesn’t benefit from a class diagram: <code>app/</code> is ~130
largely-independent, mostly-configuration-driven BlueSpice extensions
(documented structurally in [[Help:Modul/Settings.d|settings-d]] instead,
since their relationships are ''load order'', not inheritance), and the RAG
pipeline ([[Help:Modul/Haystack-Pipeline|haystack-pipeline]]) is a
declarative YAML component graph, not an object hierarchy — its natural
diagram is the <code>flowchart</code> already in that module’s doc. Force-fitting a
class diagram onto either would just restate the module docs in a worse
format.

One piece of this codebase ''is'' a genuine, useful class hierarchy: the
ChatBot extension’s <code>DeepsetApi</code> HTTP client layer
([https://github.com/Sidiberlin/hdp/blob/main/app/extensions/ChatBot/src/DeepsetApi <code>app/extensions/ChatBot/src/DeepsetApi/</code>]).
A single base class handles all outbound HTTP to <code>chatbot-proxy</code>, and six
purpose-specific subclasses each implement one REST use case. This is
worth diagramming because the shared base class is exactly what explains a
real gotcha: every subclass sends the same <code>Authorization: Bearer {apiKey}</code> header and reads the same <code>BmbfDeepsetApi*</code> config, regardless of
which specific proxy endpoint it targets.

== <code>DeepsetApi</code> Client Hierarchy ==

{{#mermaid:classDiagram
    class Connector {
        #string apiKey
        #string sessionApiUrl
        #string apiUrl
        #string indexUrl
        #string feedbackUrl
        #string tagUrl
        #string pipelineStatsUrl
        #HttpRequestFactory requestFactory
        +__construct(Config, HttpRequestFactory)
        +get(url, contentType) array
        +post(url, options, contentType) array
        +patch(url, options, contentType) array
        +delete(url, options, contentType) array
        +stream(url, options) ResponseInterface
        -executeRequest(url, options, method, contentType) ResponseInterface
    }

    class ChatApi {
        -RoleLookup roleLookup
        +request(query, sessionId, followUpType) void
        -sendSSEHeaders() void
        -getFilter() array
    }

    class SessionApi {
        +request() array
    }

    class HistoryApi {
        -FETCH_LIMIT
        +request(sessionId, after) array
    }

    class FeedbackApi {
        +request(feedbackId, after) array
        +getStats() array
        -getTagId(tag) array
    }

    class ListApi {
        -LIST_LIMIT
        +getFiles(titles) array
        -getFilter(titles) string
    }

    class IndexApi {
        -ListApi listApi
        +pushPage(indexName, contents, meta) Status
        +pushFile(filePath, meta) Status
        +batchDelete(toDelete) Status
        +purgeIndex() Status
    }

    Connector <|-- ChatApi
    Connector <|-- SessionApi
    Connector <|-- HistoryApi
    Connector <|-- FeedbackApi
    Connector <|-- ListApi
    Connector <|-- IndexApi
    IndexApi --> ListApi : uses (constructor-injected)
}}
== Notes ==

* Every subclass is wired via MediaWiki’s DI container in [https://github.com/Sidiberlin/hdp/blob/main/app/extensions/ChatBot/includes/ServiceWiring.php <code>includes/ServiceWiring.php</code>] (service names <code>DeepsetChatApi</code>, <code>DeepsetSessionApi</code>, <code>DeepsetHistoryApi</code>, <code>DeepsetFeedbackApi</code>, <code>DeepsetListApi</code>, <code>DeepsetIndexApi</code>), constructed with <code>MainConfig</code> + <code>HttpRequestFactory</code> (and, for <code>ChatApi</code>, <code>BmbfRoleLookup</code>; for <code>IndexApi</code>, <code>DeepsetListApi</code>) — not instantiated directly by callers.
* <code>ChatApi</code> is the only subclass whose <code>request()</code> writes directly to the HTTP response (<code>echo</code>/<code>ob_flush</code>/<code>flush</code>) rather than returning data — every other subclass returns an <code>array</code> (or <code>Status</code> for <code>IndexApi</code>, whose methods are also the only ones in this hierarchy actually invoked in this deployment’s day-to-day chat flow that fail silently: they’re called by the (inert here — see [[Help:Modul/ChatBot-Extension|chatbot-extension]]) <code>IndexDeepset</code> background job against an empty <code>BmbfDeepsetApiIndexUrl</code>).
* <code>Connector::executeRequest()</code> is the single chokepoint for every outbound call in this hierarchy: it always sets a <code>Bearer {apiKey}</code> Authorization header (from <code>$wgBmbfDeepsetApiKey</code>, <code>&quot;not-needed&quot;</code> in this deployment, since <code>chatbot-proxy</code> doesn’t check it) and a 120s timeout, via a freshly-constructed Guzzle <code>Client</code> per call.
